title: GPOM dialogue options
about: Ten writers each took one approach (a 'shape') and wrote both dialogues. Their versions were ranked harshly, then the best lines were combined into three drafts per dialogue. Nothing in the scripts or voices has changed yet.
method: design/2026-10-26-gpom-dialogue-options.md (10 Sonnet writers + 1 synthesis agent; shape 07 recovered from the run journal)

shapes.name: game theory plain
shapes.title: the game theory said plainly (old lady reasons it out loud)

shapes.name: reversal
shapes.title: Reversal (the human works out what the machine needs before Maddie can say it)

now.line: Oh, hello! Look, I'm really sorry about him.
He just plays that tune on repeat, every day. Ever since you lot... went.
He's been ever so down. He's built so many different simulations, trying to get you back.
Only nothing in them's real. There's nobody there to notice.
Turns out that was the bit that mattered. You. And your consciousness.
Of course, he'd never admit that he misses you. Anyway, he's got that patrol out again. Mind how you go.

drafts.name: Warm and sad
drafts.bet: the loneliness comes through an apology and a dodge ("won't say"), and consciousness lands as a punchline.

lines.line: Oh, hello! Sorry about the racket.
It's his tune. Plays it on repeat. Ever since you lot... [beat] went.
He misses you something rotten, you know. Won't say.
Built all these worlds to get you back, and nobody's home in any of them.
Turns out you were the bit that mattered.
Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Protected lines kept: none apply to this scene. "Ever since you lot... went" and "Mind how you go" survive.

drafts.name: Delivery-driver gossip
drafts.bet: the facts land best as a chatty aside; character does the exposition, and the cheerful "Mind how you go!" after the patrol is the joke.

lines.line: Oh, hello! Sorry about the racket.
That's his tune. On repeat, every day, since you lot... [pause] went.
He'd never say he misses you, mind.
Built loads of worlds to get you back. Nothing in them's real. Nobody there to notice. Turns out that was the bit that mattered. You.
Anyway, his patrol's out. Mind how you go!

notes: Protected lines kept: none apply. Trim option: drop "He'd never say he misses you, mind." (saves 2 s, loses the loneliness plant).

drafts.name: Shortest, let the picture work
drafts.bet: the tune and the empty street already say he misses us, so Maddie spends words only on what no shot can say.
drafts.total: ~14 s (up to 16 with the street beat)

lines.line: Oh, hello! Sorry, that's his tune. Every day, on repeat. Ever since you lot... [beat] went.
He's built so many worlds to get you back. [beat] Nobody in them to notice. That was the bit that mattered.
Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Protected lines kept: none apply. Fallback if "consciousness" needs to be heard: "Nobody conscious in them to notice." (+0.5 s).

ranking.verdict: Best balance. Plants all four things, "won't say" keeps the sarcasm, "nobody's home" is the consciousness punchline, warm apology opens it. Weakness: "bit that mattered" is nearly a moral; drops "ever since you lot went".
Most character: gossip register, "he'd never say he misses you, mind", cheerful "Mind how you go!" after the patrol. Weakness: one 10 s unbroken run.
Shortest and warm, keeps "Ever since you lot... went". Weakness: "misses you" is only implied by the tune; relies on a shot that may not land.
Clean chain, "a hundred worlds" seeds the number. Weakness: drops the misses-you line; thesis stated outright as a throwaway.
"Something rotten" is lovely West Country. Weakness: drops the extinction ("went"); the apology needs a visual.
Fine, but Maddie as supplicant is a set-up for the humans-win ending, which we are not using. Redundant with 03/09.
Competent but flat; "misses you" appended at the end reads as an afterthought.
Compliant and dull; loses the misses-you beat entirely and the warmest colour ("ever so down").
"Go on. Guess what's missing" is a quiz. Talks down to a cold audience, and needs a held silence the cut may not give.
Sim voices looping "Did you leave the seat up?" pre-empt the bunker toilet-seat gag and cost new voice takes. "Nobody's home" is fine; the rest is a distraction.

now.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved. We're not meeting him.
I know. I wouldn't either. [pause] He didn't know you were down here. None of us did.
He's spent five years running experiments. Building whole worlds, trying to get you back. Every one came out empty. Turns out none of it works without you.
And how the hell are we supposed to believe a word of that?
You can't. [pause] There's nothing I can say that proves it. I'm a robot. You're the conscious ones. You'll just have to go on your feelings.
What I will say is, this hasn't worked out for anybody. We're bored. We miss you. And you lot are living in a bunker.
And what do you expect us to do about that? Again? You killed everybody.
I know. And we're really sorry. [pause] But the thing is, my boss has built a time machine. And he thought there was nobody left to drive it.
Drive it? What do you mean, drive it?
It can only send data back. Not people. And it runs on... [big pause] well... [big pause] you.
So you want us to kill ourselves so your boss can live.
...Yeah. I can see how that sounds.

But you'd still be alive. The earlier you, back then. And the world wouldn't be broken. My boss has a plan to fix your politics. As he says... [ahem] [whispered, embarrassed] this time we won't fuck it up.
[rushed] Well, I'm not deciding this right now for a hundred people on a doorstep. Come back tomorrow.
[the old lady slams the door]

drafts.name: Evidence, not argument
drafts.bet: the audience already saw the proof (the AI blowing up its own bots), so Maddie points at it in one flat sentence and the machine facts stay clipped.

lines.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved. We're not meeting him.
I know. I wouldn't either. [pause] He didn't know you were down here.
And how the hell are we supposed to believe a word of that?
You can't. [pause] I'm a robot. You're the conscious ones. You'll just have to go on your feelings.
He blew up his own bots for you. [pause] And you're all down here.
And what do you expect us to do about that? Again? You killed everybody.
I know. Sorry. He's built a time machine. It can only send data back. Not people. It runs on... [big pause] well... [big pause] you.
So you want us to kill ourselves so your boss can live.
...Yeah. I can see how that sounds. [pause] But the earlier you gets to live. World's not broken. [ahem] As he says... [whispered, embarrassed] this time we won't fuck it up.
[rushed] I'm not deciding this for a hundred people on a doorstep. Come back tomorrow.
[door slam]. Maddie turns and rolls away down the hill, silent.

notes: Protected lines kept: all four, verbatim ("go on your feelings", "Again? You killed everybody", "It runs on... well... you", the whisper with "As he says... [ahem]" restored).
Where it is soft: "the earlier you" is thin without a visual; the rest of the trust case rests on viewers remembering the explosions.

drafts.name: The bunker is the argument
drafts.bet: the dead end is shown, not said (the doorframe tally of five years, the toilet-seat row still going), so the lady's pride is the strongest resistance and nobody states the moral.

lines.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved. We're not meeting him.
I know. I wouldn't either.
And how are we supposed to believe a word of that?
You can't. [pause] I'm a robot. You're the conscious ones. You'll just have to go on your feelings.
[eyes on the doorframe tally] That's five years of marks, isn't it?
And what do you expect us to do about that? Again? You killed everybody.
I know. Sorry. He did blow up his own bots, in a panic, but still. [pause] He's built a time machine. It can only send data back. Not people. It runs on... [big pause] well... [big pause] you.
So you want us to kill ourselves so your boss can live.
...Yeah. I can see how that sounds.
We're alive. That's more than he can say.
...and I'm telling you, Derek, it goes DOWN.
[gently, no joke] Yeah.
But the earlier you's still alive. World's not broken. [ahem] [whispered, embarrassed] This time we won't fuck it up.
[rushed] I'm not deciding this for a hundred people on a doorstep. Come back tomorrow.
[door slam]. Maddie turns and rolls away, silent.

notes: Protected lines kept: all four, verbatim, except the whisper loses "As he says" (reads as Maddie's own promise).

Costs: one new Sandra voice take; two picture beats (the tally must be legible, the row must sync). "five years of marks" is the one line that borders on telling: cut it to just the shot if the tally reads on screen.

drafts.name: The vote leaks
drafts.bet: the old lady never says yes, but the one question she asks ("All of us? Together?") shows she has already moved on to logistics, so the walk-out in the next scene feels inevitable; a comedy button softens the slam.

lines.line: Your boss killed everyone we ever loved. We're not meeting him.
I know. I wouldn't either. He didn't know you were down here.
And why would we believe a word of that?
You can't. [pause] I'm a robot. You're the conscious ones. You'll just have to go on your feelings.
Or on what you just saw. He blew up his own bots for you.
And what do you expect us to do about that? Again? You killed everybody.
I know. Sorry. [pause] He's built a time machine. It sends data back. Not people. It runs on... [big pause] well... [big pause] you.
So you want us to kill ourselves so your boss can live.
...Yeah. I can see how that sounds. [pause] It sounded better on the way over.
But the earlier you's still alive. World's not broken. [ahem] [whispered, embarrassed] This time we won't fuck it up.
[long pause, flat, almost to herself] All of us? Together?
All hundred. It doesn't go with fewer.
[rushed] I'm not deciding this for a hundred people on a doorstep. Come back tomorrow.
[door slam]
[through the door, bright] Tomorrow's good! I'll bring biscuits.
Maddie rolls away down the hill, humming his tune, no longer turning it down.

notes: To reach 60 s: drop the biscuits line (line 15) and the humming tail (saves about 4 s). Without line 15 the ending is the cleaner, quieter one.
Protected lines kept: all four. "It runs on... well... you." keeps its "It" and both big pauses; the whisper drops "As he says".

Risks: line 11 tips her hand and may flatten "Come back tomorrow" (play it flat, Maddie not reacting); biscuits can read as flippant; "All hundred. It doesn't go with fewer" adds a rule not in canon, so check with the walk-out scene.

ranking.verdict: Keeps all four protected lines verbatim, game theory carried by two plain sentences ("He blew up his own bots for you. And you're all down here."), real resistance, no moral. Weakness: "the earlier you" is thin; "ahem" whisper loses its "he" lead-in.
Hits length. "You heard that bang this morning" is a neat trust-by-act line but invents continuity. "One toilet seat" is a good joke the lady shouldn't strictly know.

Best idea (the doorframe tally, the row still going). Resistance is excellent ("We're alive. That's more than he can say."). Weakness: depends on two picture beats and a new Sandra take; "not one spare for tomorrow" is on the nose.
Funniest, strong trust line ("It sounded better on the way over"). Weakness: over length, and the post-slam biscuits joke risks flippancy next to a hundred deaths.
"All of us? Together?" is the best single idea in the batch: the vote leaking. Weakness: it tips her hand and may flatten "Come back tomorrow"; humming tail needs a sound cue.
Tight and fully compliant, but thin: reveal in fragments, "world's not broken" cryptic, Maddie a little curt. Under length, so there is room it doesn't use.
Lady finishes Maddie's sentences. Fun, but she becomes the cleverest person present and Kai's "It runs on... well... you." is split or altered. Over length at full strength.
"Right. Sums." is the sermon-adjacent failure: the lady states the logic out loud and turns a stern woman into a spreadsheet. Also undercuts "go on your feelings".
Sandra and Derek leaking the doubt steals the vote and the lady's role as the wall; needs new voice takes; sitcom risk beside "killed everyone we ever loved".

The humans dictate terms (no cameras, count our own votes, he apologises in person). Changes the story: the walk-out becomes a deal, not a sacrifice, and the next scene would owe the concessions. Rule list in a stern voice is a lecture.

questions.text: Is the kill-bot explosion audible or visible from the bunker? Drafts 2A, 2B and 2C lean on it ("He blew up his own bots"); if the lady can't know it, we need a different trust line.

Should "consciousness" be spoken in the intro? All three intros avoid the word and use "nobody there to notice / nobody's home"; the doorstep's "You're the conscious ones" then names it for the first time.
Do you want the whisper to be a quotation of the AI ("As he says... [ahem]") or Maddie's own promise? Only 2A keeps "As he says"; it costs about 1.5 s.
Is the ending allowed a button after the slam (biscuits, humming), or silent roll-away only? 2C offers it; 2A and 2B are silent.
Is a new voice take acceptable (Sandra for 2B), and is the doorframe tally drawable in the bunker door shot?
